item.title: 1.0.0-rc2
item.description:
The first public release. Everything below arrived in phases 0–15; it is listed here once, by what it does rather than by when it was built.

The panels

  • Two panels with tabs, folder tree, brief and full listings, quick search by name, quick filter, navigation history, favourite folders.
  • Tabs can be locked to a folder: wander off freely, and coming back to the tab brings the folder back with it.
  • Panels side by side or one above the other.
  • Colour rules — mask, age, size, files or folders — with the first matching rule deciding. Marked and hidden entries keep their own colours.
  • The branch (⌃B): every file below the current folder in one flat list, each named by its path, with the ordinary commands working on it.
  • Folder sizes on demand, select by mask, invert, by extension, and a selection that can be put aside and brought back.

Files

  • F5–F8 through a real operation engine: progress, conflicts, cancellation, a background queue, and copyfile(3) on the local disk.
  • Delete to the Trash, delete permanently, or overwrite-then-delete — the last one saying plainly what that is worth on an SSD.
  • Multi-rename with patterns and counters, attributes and timestamps, split and join, checksums (SHA-256, BLAKE3) created and verified.
  • Compare two folders, and synchronize them: a direction per pair, optional deletion of extras, and a verification pass afterwards.
  • Compare two files line by line, with the changed part of a changed line highlighted, encodings, and honest answers for binaries and giants.

Archives

  • ZIP and TAR read and written by us; RAR and 7z read through the system's bsdtar. An archive behaves like a folder in the panel.
  • Encrypted ZIP: ZipCrypto and AES-256 read without ever putting the password on a command line, and packing with AES-256. Passwords live in the session, or in the Keychain if you tick the box.

Finding things

  • Search by name, mask, size, date, content — as text or as a regular expression — optionally inside archives, with locked archives counted rather than silently skipped.
  • Saved searches, and a duplicate finder that decides by content and never offers to select a whole group.

The rest

  • Built-in viewer (text, hex, image) with encodings and search; a command line at the bottom; a real terminal pane below the panels.
  • SFTP: a server behaves like a folder, with the same keys as the disk.
  • A button bar and user commands, and every command rebindable to the key you want.
  • Six languages: English, Slovenian, German, French, Italian, Russian.

Trying, buying, updating

  • Everything works for 30 days. After that the app keeps browsing, searching, viewing, comparing and checksums; copying, moving, deleting and the other commands that change files need a licence — one line above the panels says so, without nagging.
  • A licence is €9.99 once, covers every 1.x version, and is checked on the Mac itself: the key arrives by e-mail, is pasted under Help → Licence…, and works without the internet.
  • Updates through Sparkle: the app asks once whether it may look for them, and never installs one without you.
  • The app sends nothing anywhere — no telemetry, no usage counts — except the update check you agreed to.

Known limits

  • Listing uses FileManager rather than getattrlistbulk(2): correct on SMB and NFS too, but folders past ~20,000 entries show it.
  • No plugins (Total Commander's are Windows DLLs), no FTP or WebDAV, no custom columns or thumbnails, no printing. Each is recorded, with its reason, in docs/faza-15-nacrt.md.
  • Full Disk Access must be granted by hand for ~/Library, other applications' data and Time Machine; macOS offers no way to ask for it. The app says so at first launch and again when a listing is refused.
